sermon.title: Success in Tragedies Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor Kincer
sermon.summary: Daniel is more than the lions’ den. He endured captivity as his nation rejected God—killing prophets and burning Jeremiah’s scroll. America trades truth for positive thinking. Daniel never blamed God and stayed faithful through his training.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

chunks.section_question: What do we hear about Daniel?
chunks.short_answer: The lions’ den and more—but scripture is written for our understanding.
chunks.text:
We hear a lot about the book of Daniel. We hear about the lions’ den. We hear about the fiery furnace. We hear all kinds of scriptures being used to connect to the end time. But have you ever really thought about how Daniel got to the place where God used him? And that’s in chapter 1. Most people just zip over chapter 1 to get to the other stuff. And I want to remind you that the Bible tells us in Romans 15:4 that all things that were written up before time of were written for our learning. That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

So, when you go to the scriptures, they’re written for you to get understanding, to get learning. 1 Corinthians 10:11, all these things happened unto them, Israel. And they are written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the world are come. And so, when we read the Old Testament, we got to say, “God, what am I supposed to learn for today?” 2 Timothy 3:16, all scripture is given by the inspiration of God and is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness. That the man of God may be complete, mature, and furnished unto all good works. And so, Genesis to Malachi, Matthew to Revelation is written for us to learn, folks. Not just to read, but it’s to learn.

And so, with that mentality, let’s take a look at Daniel. And I’m going to call this first session the characteristics for success in tragedies. Okay? If you’ve lived any time on this earth, you’ve encountered tragedies. You’ve encountered difficulties. Or my second title is how to be a successful teenager. So, in Daniel 1, we have the tragedies. We have the difficulties. Number one, in Daniel 1:1, Jerusalem is besieged. We have a story in 2 Kings chapter 6 where Jerusalem was besieged before. An army circuited about, no food could get in, nobody could get out, no one could go in, and slowly the people would starve to death.

Okay? People would eat people. It says in 2 Kings 6, they would eat their babies that were born. They would eat the placenta that came out after the baby was born. They would eat dung. That’s how hungry. That’s what a siege is. They would eat horses, dogs, whatever was there, they would eat. And then there was nothing left to eat. A siege is a serious thing. And this siege in Daniel lasted about 8 years. That was a long time. And Daniel was about 17 years old when he was taken to the land of Babylon. And we know this because number one, he wasn’t in the military. And at 20, everybody goes to the military in the Old Testament.

You know, if there was a God then these bad stuff wouldn’t go on. There wouldn’t be wars or not. God said there would be. Have you read your book?
